verdict.rationale: Pipecat documents Smart Turn Detection, which uses a machine learning model to decide when a user has finished speaking. It reads intonation and linguistic cues rather than relying only on a silence timeout, and turn detection also accounts for STT latency. That is model-based end-of-turn detection beyond plain VAD. Missing for 10: hands-on or independent corroboration, documentation of configuration and tuning options, and explicit evidence that it holds up with slow or pausing speakers.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use model-based end-of-turn detection beyond simple VAD silence timeouts so the agent doesn't talk over slow speakers

citations.quote: Smart Turn Detection uses an advanced machine learning model to determine when a user has finished speaking and your bot should respond.
Smart Turn Detection recognizes natural conversational cues like intonation patterns and linguistic signals for more natural conversations.
Pipecat ships with measured P99 latency values for each supported service so that turn detection can account for this delay automatically.
